description: Whitewashed stone gone patchy closes both sides and a low beam roof with bales stacked into it closes overhead; a swept plank floor polished pale underfoot, hand shears hanging by their bow on a nail, a wisp of wool caught on every nail head down the wall.

Tarred feather-edge wall boards down both sides under corrugated tin on a timber frame with the rafters showing, the shed's own walls closing the frame; a green enamel kettle and two enamel mugs on a shelf, bright blue and orange twine at every hurdle joint.

Breeze-block to waist height and feather-edge boards above, the roof closing overhead in bare corrugated tin; a coiled rope on a nail, a galvanised bucket gone chalky hanging by its handle, a heap of loose wool reading warm oatmeal and dusty cream on the swept plank floor.

Whitewashed stone walls gone butter-yellow with age closing both sides, a beam ceiling with bales stacked up into it closing overhead; the clippers hanging on their cord from a beam, a bound bundle of wool tied round with orange twine leaning at the base of the wall.

Corrugated tin on a timber frame with the rafters showing, the shed's own walls boarding up both sides and closing the frame; a besom broom stood in a drift of loose wool, a pitchfork stood against the wall boards, the swept plank floor polished pale underfoot.

Tarred feather-edge wall boards closing down both sides under a corrugated tin roof, bright bands of light coming between the boards; an open-topped wooden crate with dusty cream wool spilling over the rim, a hank of blue twine on a nail with one end trailing.

Whitewashed stone gone patchy closing both sides under a beam roof with straw bales stacked into it; a wooden chair with a coat over the back of it near the door, an enamel mug forgotten on a rail with wool stuck round its pale green base.

Breeze-block to waist height and silvered boards above, the shed's own roof closing in bare tin overhead; a halter looped over the top hurdle rail, straw bales up into the rafters, the swept plank floor polished pale by years of feet.

Tarred feather-edge wall boards down both sides and corrugated tin closing the frame overhead; two broad cream-woolled grown sheep pressed against a hurdle pen, their combined height just reaching the second hurdle rail, a heap of oatmeal-toned loose wool beside them on the swept plank floor.

Whitewashed stone gone patchy on both sides, the beam roof with bales stacked up closing overhead; the timber door jamb framing a hazy patch of pale yard beyond, that returning light laid as a bright band across the swept plank floor inside, a heap of loose wool glowing warm oatmeal in it.

Corrugated tin on a timber frame with rafters showing, the shed walls closing both sides; the open end's own wide timber lintel framing the yard small and soft beyond, that outside light coming back in across the nearest hurdle rail and the oatmeal heap of wool below it.

Feather-edge boards down both sides gone silvery with age, a low corrugated tin roof overhead closing the frame; the doorway's own stone jamb thick with lime, the yard blurred and small beyond it, and the light returning from that opening laid as a pale band across the swept plank floor.

Whitewashed stone walls gone butter-yellow closing both sides, the beam ceiling with bales stacked into it closing overhead; the shed's own timber-framed door propped open, the hurdle across its sill, green hedge visible small and hazy beyond, that light bringing warmth back onto a sheep's newly-bared pale cream back inside.

Breeze-block to waist height and tarred boards above, corrugated tin closing overhead; the door's own timber jamb part of the room's front wall, the packed-earth yard seen through it softer and much smaller, that light returning to lie as a bright flat band across the swept plank floor close to the threshold.

Feather-edge wall boards closing the frame on both sides, a beam roof with bales stacked up into it overhead; the open end's own wide board surround framing the hazy yard beyond, outside light coming back in to rest on the loose wool heap and light its oatmeal and dusty-cream tones.

Corrugated tin on a timber frame with bare rafters showing overhead, whitewashed stone piers closing the corners; a leaning stack of spare hurdles against one wall, a galvanised bucket gone chalky beside them, the swept plank floor polished pale by years of feet stretching to the back wall.

Tarred feather-edge wall boards closing both sides under corrugated tin, bright bands of light between the boards; a loose mob of broad cream-woolled grown sheep filling the hurdle pen, their woolly backs at the height of the second rail, the swept plank floor pale beneath them.

Whitewashed stone walls gone patchy closing both sides, a low beam ceiling with bales stacked into it overhead; hand shears hanging by their bow on a nail, a coiled rope beside them on the same wall, a drift of loose oatmeal-toned wool along the base of the wall.

Breeze-block to waist height and feather-edge boards above, bare corrugated tin closing the frame overhead; a speckle-nosed grown sheep and two blocky black-faced grown sheep in a loose uneven group in the hurdle pen, one set apart and nosing the swept plank floor, the others pressing together at the hurdle rail.

Tarred feather-edge wall boards going silvery on both sides, a corrugated tin roof on a timber frame with rafters showing overhead; the clippers hanging on their cord from a central beam, a bound bundle of wool tied round with bright orange twine on the swept plank floor beneath them.

Whitewashed stone gone butter-yellow with age closing both sides under a beam ceiling with bales stacked up into it; a wooden chair with a coat over its back, a green enamel kettle and two enamel mugs on a plank shelf, a wisp of wool on every nail head down the wall.

Feather-edge boards closing the frame on both sides, corrugated tin overhead with the rafters showing plainly; a loose uneven mob of grown sheep spread across the hurdle pen, two pressing at the far rail and one standing apart, all well above the height of the bottom rail, all wearing heavy wool coats.

Whitewashed stone walls gone patchy closing both sides, a low beam roof with straw bales stacked into it overhead; an open-topped wooden crate with dusty cream wool spilling over the rim, a pitchfork stood against the boards beside it, the swept plank floor polished pale underfoot.

Breeze-block to waist height and tarred boards closing the frame above it on both sides, corrugated tin on timber rafters overhead; a halter of worn leather looped over a hurdle rail, a hank of blue twine on the nail above it, a heap of loose warm-oatmeal wool on the swept plank floor.

A dry stone wall with moss thick on its north side, nettles tall along its foot; a yard gate painted chalky blue hung on a rope hinge, a water trough brimming at one corner, a race of hurdles tied with bright blue twine funnelling to the shed door.

Grass worn to bare packed earth through the gateway, a chalky galvanised bucket hanging by its handle on the faded blue gate, the hawthorn hedge grown thick and shaggy closing the frame behind the pens.

A dry stone wall with moss deep on its north side closes behind the hurdle race, a coiled rope on the gatepost, nettles tall along the wall's foot, bright blue and orange twine knotted at every hurdle joint.

The shed's own limewashed gable gone butter-yellow stands close behind the pens, a besom broom leant against it, a bound bundle of wool tied round with orange twine sitting out on sunk uneven flagstones.
A race of hurdles tied with bright orange twine funnels to the shed door, a halter looped over the top rail, the dry stone wall with moss thick down its shaded side closing the whole frame behind.

Flagstones sunk and uneven by the trough, a green enamel mug forgotten on the gatepost with a tuft of warm oatmeal wool stuck round its base, the shed's own gable in limewash gone butter-yellow standing close behind.

A lane worn pale along the wall line, a pitchfork stood against the dry stone wall, a heap of loose wool in dusty cream caught against the bottom of the hurdle gate, the hawthorn hedge thick and shaggy closing behind.
A gap in the dry stone wall shut with a single hurdle, bright blue twine at its corners, a hank of orange twine on a nail with one end trailing, nettles tall along the wall's foot behind the pen.

A stone step hollowed in the middle at the shed door, an open-topped wooden crate with warm oatmeal wool spilling over the rim beside it, the shed's limewashed gable gone butter-yellow closing the frame directly behind.

A water trough brimming at one corner, flagstones sunk and uneven around its base, a chalky galvanised bucket hung by its handle on the stone wall's iron pin, the dry stone wall with deep green moss closing behind the pens.

A yard gate on a rope hinge painted faded blue, iron strap hinges worn silver-bright, a bound bundle of wool tied with bright orange twine on the flags beneath it, the shaggy hawthorn hedge standing close behind.
